nodes.summary: The index pairs `(i, j)` with `i + j + 2 ≤ n`; the pair stands for the unit triangle with vertices `(i + 1, j)`, `(i, j + 1)` and `(i + 1, j + 1)`. Together with the up cells they triangulate the triangle with corners `(0, 0)`, `(n, 0)` and `(0, n)` into `n²` unit triangles.
nodes.title: Down cells of the grid triangulation

nodes.summary: Every Sperner colouring of the grid triangle with corners `(0, 0)`, `(n, 0)` and `(0, n)` has a rainbow cell: an up cell `{(i, j), (i + 1, j), (i, j + 1)}` or a down cell `{(i + 1, j), (i, j + 1), (i + 1, j + 1)}` whose three vertices carry the three colours. Immediate from the parity form `odd_card_rainbow` (Sperner 1928, two-dimensional case, for the grid triangulation).
nodes.title: Sperner's lemma in dimension two

nodes.summary: Three colours in `{0, 1, 2}` are pairwise distinct, so that a cell with these vertex colours is fully labelled.
nodes.title: Rainbow triple of colours

nodes.summary: A colouring `c i j ∈ {0, 1, 2}` of the grid points of the triangle with corners `(0, 0)`, `(n, 0)` and `(0, n)` such that points on the bottom side (`j = 0`) avoid colour `2`, points on the left side (`i = 0`) avoid colour `1`, and points on the hypotenuse (`i + j = n`) avoid colour `0`. The corners are then forced to have colours `0`, `1` and `2` (for `n ≥ 1`; for `n = 0` no colouring qualifies).
nodes.title: Sperner colouring of the grid triangle

nodes.summary: Colour the points `0, 1, …, n` with two colours so that `c 0 = 0` and `c n = 1`. Then the number of indices `i < n` with `c i ≠ c (i + 1)` (bichromatic unit segments) is odd; in particular there is at least one.
nodes.title: Sperner's lemma in dimension one

nodes.summary: For every Sperner colouring `c` of the grid triangle with corners `(0, 0)`, `(n, 0)` and `(0, n)` (`IsSpernerColouring`), the number of rainbow cells of the grid triangulation, up cells plus down cells, is odd.
nodes.title: Sperner's lemma in dimension two (parity form)

nodes.summary: The index pairs `(i, j)` with `i + j < n`; the pair stands for the unit triangle with vertices `(i, j)`, `(i + 1, j)` and `(i, j + 1)`.
nodes.title: Up cells of the grid triangulation

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
